function: Multi-agent PPO policy jointly sets each UAV's sensing/communication power split, communication sub-channel, and next position in a joint radar-communication swarm (pp. 6, 9).
system: 5 JRC UAVs, 3 targets; sensing main beam plus communication sub-beam, antenna count not stated, 13 dBi gains; no RIS; 3 GHz, eight 1 MHz channels (pp. 4, 10).
method: Multi-agent PPO actor-critic (RLCTDT) with RNN layers, entropy regularization, centralized training and distributed execution; online reinforcement learning in a simulated environment, 4,000,000 training steps (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Self-built simulator: line-of-sight UAV-UAV free-space channel gain, radar-equation sensing SNR, 0.25 m2 target cross-section; no dataset or standard channel model (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Same 5-UAV, 3-target scenario for training (4,000,000 steps) and testing; sweeps of rate threshold, detection SNR threshold, UAV count; UAV failure case; no stated train-test shift (pp. 10-15).
baselines: RLCTDT-KL (multi-agent PPO-KL), IRLCTDT (independent per-UAV RLCTDT), Random actions, and RLCTDT without RNNs; no classical optimization baseline (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Episode reward, sensing reward, guidance reward, punitive negative reward, convergence curves; 16% higher stabilized reward than RLCTDT-KL (pp. 10-15).
complexity: Big-O training complexity of RNN and MLP layers in actor and critic, scaling with episodes, time steps, UAVs and layer sizes (p. 10); no FLOPs or runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "the communication is treated as a line-of-sight (LoS) channel" - free-space gain of Eq. (11) and radar-equation SNR of Eq. (9) in a custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "scenario under the same environment" - the UAV failure test (Figs. 10-11) is run in the same environment, and the sweeps of Figs. 12-14 are not stated to differ from training; the paper never says a trained policy is tested on unseen conditions or retrained per setting.
q3_support: p. 10: "RLCTDT-KL: This is the multi-agent version of PPO-KL" built in alignment with the paper's own algorithm structure, so it is a variant of the proposed method; p. 10: "Random: All UAVs randomly select an action at each time" is the only non-learned baseline; no earlier published learned method for this task is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "we perform theoretical analysis of the complexity of the RLCTDT algorithm" - the overall training complexity is a big-O expression in episodes, time steps, UAVs, and RNN and MLP layer sizes.
q5_support: p. 10: "we construct a virtual simulation environment" - self-built simulator with no code or data link, no public dataset, and no measured data; p. 15 lists real-world testing as ongoing work.
notes: Area 6 rather than 5: the learned policy controls the sensing/communication power split and channel allocation of aerial UAV links jointly with trajectories (p. 6, Eq. 27), and 6 outranks 5 in the tie-break order; above_phy passes under the joint physical-layer plus above rule. Antenna count is not stated (admitted for NTN). Borderline q3: RLCTDT-KL, IRLCTDT and the no-RNN version are all variants of the proposed algorithm, so only Random is an independent baseline; reviewer may count RLCTDT-KL as standard PPO-KL. Borderline q2: the UAV failure test (pp. 13-14) is the only candidate shift, but the paper does not state it was absent from training.
